```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6)
library(repair)
stopifnot(requireNamespace("nlme", quietly = TRUE))
```

## Assess the information behind an analysis

Random-Effect Prediction Adjustment for Inference in Regression
(REPAIR) reports posterior reliability for the random coefficients selected by
the structural formula and provides tables of sample, score, and numerical
diagnostics. These are descriptive checks, not automatic tests of whether an
analysis is adequate. Numerical convergence alone does not establish strong
information or reliable inference.

This executable example uses a synthetic reproduction dataset with unequal
observation counts, AR(1) residual correlation, and phase-specific residual SDs.
An ordinary analysis supplies its own measurement models and person-level table.

```{r fit}
case <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "nlme-workflow-reference.rds",
                           package = "repair"))$cases$both_ar1_ident
measurement <- nlme::lme(y ~ z, random = ~ z | id, data = case$data,
  correlation = nlme::corAR1(form = ~ time | id),
  weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~ 1 | phase),
  control = nlme::lmeControl(msMaxIter = 300))
fit <- repair(re("z", "growth") ~ re("(Intercept)", "growth"),
  list(growth = measurement), case$people, "id")
summary(fit)
```

The summary labels effect roles so the predictor-side reliability emphasized in
the paper is easy to identify. Reliability does not modify scores, covariances,
regularization, coefficients, or standard errors.

## Two distinct uncertainty calculations

For a selected random coefficient k, marginal posterior reliability for person i is

\[
\rho_{ik}=1-\frac{V_{i,kk}}{G_{kk}}, \qquad
V_i=G-GZ_i^\top(R_i+Z_iGZ_i^\top)^{-1}Z_iG.
\]

Here G is the fitted random-effect covariance, Z_i is the effective random-effect
design, and R_i is the fitted residual covariance. This calculation uses all
random coefficients within that measurement model. It supports a singular G
without inverting it. It conditions on fitted parameters.

V_i is a **posterior covariance**. REPAIR's structural estimator instead uses
likelihood-only scores and their **sampling-error covariance**. These are different
quantities. Do not replace the estimator's error inputs with posterior variances.
A cluster with an unidentifiable likelihood-only slope can still have a defined
posterior reliability because its posterior also uses G; that does not rescue its
failed likelihood-only score for structural analysis.

For an intercept/slope model, the slope component residualized on the intercept is
\(u_1-G_{01}u_0/G_{00}\). With \(a=(-G_{01}/G_{00},1)^\top\), its reliability is
\(1-a^\top V_i a/(a^\top G a)\). This is the manuscript's residualized diagnostic;
it uses off-diagonal covariance and does not condition on other structural
predictors or on another measurement process. It is available only for selected
slopes in two-coefficient random-intercept/random-slope models in this release.

```{r reliability}
r <- repair_reliability(fit)
r[, c("model", "term", "role", "measure", "reliability", "n_people", "n_defined")]
person <- repair_reliability(fit, level = "person")
head(person[, c("id", "term", "measure", "n_observations", "prior_variance",
               "posterior_variance", "reliability")])
```

The default `type = "both"` reports marginal reliability for every selected
effect and residualized reliability where applicable. `type = "marginal"` selects
only marginal values. With `type = "residualized"`, an inapplicable selected
effect receives an explicit status and reason instead of disappearing.

## Cohorts and undefined values

By default the cohort consists of the **analyzed people**, equally weighted.
The aggregate is the arithmetic mean of their person-specific reliabilities,
matching the manuscript's empirical formula. It is not weighted by observation
count or by the structural estimator's inverse-variance weights.

```{r cohorts}
# Compare the same measurement fit across different structural cohorts.
subset_fit <- repair(re("z", "growth") ~ re("(Intercept)", "growth"),
  list(growth = measurement), case$people[1:40, ], "id")
repair_reliability(subset_fit)[, c("term", "measure", "cohort", "n_people", "reliability")]
repair_reliability(subset_fit, cohort = "measurement")[,
  c("term", "measure", "cohort", "n_people", "reliability")]
```

`cohort = "measurement"` includes all effective grouping levels, separately for
each referenced model. It can include people excluded from structural analysis.
In multiple-model analyses, analyzed-cohort summaries use the same people for all
models; measurement-cohort denominators may differ. Reliability is computed within
each measurement model and does not borrow information across models or infer
anything from the cross-model scoring-error policy.

A zero or numerically degenerate prior contrast variance makes the reliability
ratio undefined. Singularity of G alone does not make every marginal ratio
undefined. Rows record `status` and `reason`; no undefined ratio is converted to
zero reliability. If any requested reliability is undefined, the overall
`reliability` is NA. `mean_defined` is a separately labeled mean over defined
values, with `n_defined` and `n_undefined` exposing its denominator. Person-level
rows retain posterior computation failures. Tiny excursions beyond zero or one
within 1e-8 are rounded to the boundary; larger excursions remain undefined with
a reason. No substantive reliability cutoff is imposed.

## Plot heterogeneity

```{r reliability-distribution}
plot(person)
```

```{r reliability-observations}
plot(person, type = "observations", pch = 19)
```

Panels identify model, coefficient, and measure. Subtitles identify the cohort
and defined/total counts. These plots do not imply that observation count alone
determines reliability: time design, residual structure, and variance components
also matter. Undefined rows are not drawn and remain visible in the counts.

## Inspect structural diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
d <- repair_diagnostics(fit)
d$cohort
d$measurement
d$excluded
d$score_failures
d$regularization
d$conditioning
d$weight_summary
head(d$weights)
head(d$error_variances)
```

- `cohort` and `excluded` explain which people entered the structural fit.
  `score_failures` identifies the model, ID, reason, and inclusion status, including
  failed scores outside the analyzed cohort.
- `error_variances` lists the input-scale likelihood-only error variances for
  structural outcomes and predictor columns. Observed variables have zero error
  under the model's assumptions. Full covariances remain in `fit@analysis_data`.
- `regularization` shows policy, alpha, and the error-subtraction multiplier for
  each moment step. A multiplier of one means full error subtraction. Disabling
  regularization does not disable measurement-error correction.
- `conditioning` describes the preliminary and final corrected predictor moments,
  including the structural intercept. Condition numbers depend on predictor units;
  these raw values are not invariant adequacy scores. A nonpositive minimum
  eigenvalue gives an infinite condition number.
- `weights` contains analyzed IDs, inverse case-variance weights, and their fractions.
  `weight_equivalent_n = 1 / sum(fraction^2)` describes weight concentration;
  it is neither an inferential sample size nor degrees of freedom.
- `reliability` contains the analyzed-cohort reliability table, and
  `cross_model_error` preserves the policy and supplied blocks.

On numerical structural failure, `status` reports the failed step and message.
Measurement and cohort diagnostics remain usable. Structural diagnostic tables
whose intermediate state is unavailable have zero rows; they do not fabricate
partial estimates. These diagnostics do not propagate measurement-model or
covariance-estimation uncertainty and do not establish nominal coverage for a
particular dataset.

For a single diagnostic table, use `repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "weights")`
or another exact table name. The existing list interface above remains available.
Use `repair_coefficients(fit)` for a structural reporting table, `repair_scores(fit)`
for ID-keyed scores and sampling-error SDs, and `repair_score_covariance(fit)` for
correlated scoring errors. See `vignette("extracting-results")` for safe joins
between score and reliability tables.

## Reproducibility

Frozen reliability fixtures were generated without loading `repair`, using the
companion simulation's posterior covariance, marginal reliability, contrast
reliability, and residualized slope helpers. Tests refit balanced, unbalanced,
and AR(1)/heteroskedastic measurement models, and also check lmer posterior
variances against `ranef(condVar = TRUE)`. Separate tests cover singular priors,
rank-deficient clusters, cohort selection, multiple models, failed structural
fits, and reconstruction of structural moment diagnostics. Existing REPAIR
coefficient/SE reference tests remain unchanged.
